courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Professional Writing and Editing
courses.description: Advanced practice with writing for professional audiences, based on attention to theories of genre, audience, rhetoric, and style. Students will develop skills in professional writing, editing, copyediting, proofreading, and publishing.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Professional Writing in Health and Medicine (Interdisciplinary)
courses.description: Advanced practice with writing about health from medical and humanistic perspectives, ranging from grant proposals to qualitative research articles to the personal illness narrative.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Professional Writing in the Arts
courses.description: A course focused on writing in professional settings focused on the arts and humanities. Students will compose documents such as funding proposals, performance reviews, artists' statements, or promotional educational materials. Includes oral, written, and digital compositions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Professional Communication for Social Movements
courses.description: Advanced course focused on writing for professional audiences in non-profit, public policy, social justice, and social entrepreneurship settings. Includes oral, written, and digital compositions. Students will compose documents such as grant proposals, policy reports, websites, public presentations, or multimedia videos to advance social causes.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Scientific and Technical Communication
courses.description: Advanced course focused on adapting scientific and technical content to public or non-expert audiences in oral, written, and digital forms. Assignments may include composing professional reports, developing multimedia instructions for a product, or developing an interactive exhibit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Business Communication
courses.description: Advanced practice with business and professional oral, written, and multimedia forms. Students will develop business proposals, reports, plans, and professional oral presentations for professional audiences.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Legal Communication
courses.description: Advanced practice with oral, written, and digital composition for legal settings.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Playwriting
courses.description: A workshop for people interested in writing plays, focusing on elements that make them work on stage, such as characterization, climax, dialogue, exposition, momentum, setting, and visual effects.

source.text: ENGL 306. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENGL 130 , 131 , 132H , or 133H . | FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Fiction and Poetry: Stylistics
courses.description: An occasional intermediate course that may focus on such topics as living writers, poetic forms, flash fiction, or imitation. Permission of the program director.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: ENGL 307. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENGL 130 , 131 , 132H , or 133H . | FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Gram-O-Rama: Grammar in Performance
courses.description: Studies of syntax, parts of speech, types of sentences, wordplay, the narrative and non-narrative power of words, prose style, and the relationships between language, rhythm, and culture culminate with students performing a selection of the comedic and dramatic sketches written during the semester.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Fairy Tales
courses.description: A study of fairy tales as historical artifacts that reveal the concerns of their times and places, as narrative structures capable of remarkable transformation, and as artistic performances drawing upon the expressive resources of multiple media, intended to challenge conventional presuppositions about the genre.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Oral Presentations in the Professional World
courses.description: Students will focus on learning skills and strategies to deliver effective oral presentations. The course will be organized around an individual research project that will culminate in a major presentation following the "best practices" of that discipline. During the semester, students will deliver presentations of various lengths and genres and will learn effective use of media support. Course standards will emphasize professional-level expectations and current "best practices" in the field. Honors version available.

source.text: ENGL 312. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENGL 105 or ENGL 105I . | COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Writing and Social Networks
courses.description: This class explores writing in and about contemporary social media spaces. The course focuses on developing writing projects that study and participate in online social networks. Topics include the rhetoric of the Internet; collaboration online; information ethics; amateur content creation; networks and social interaction; networks and literacy; data and privacy; and remix composition.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Multimedia Composition
courses.description: This class studies composing in a variety of modes, including visuals, moving images, gestures, sounds, and words. Students develop projects using image, audio, and video editors, examining how multimedia fits within the history of rhetoric and writing and relates with concerns such as purposes, audiences, contexts, arguments, genres, and mediums. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Cinema of the 1970s: New Hollywood and Beyond
courses.description: This course examines one of the most adventurous decades in U.S. film history, from the "Auteur Renaissance," to independent cinema, through to the politically conscious reconfiguration of popular genres. Films are discussed in the context of social changes and anxieties in the years surrounding Watergate and the Vietnam War.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creating the Video Essay
courses.description: This instructional course gives students the opportunity to make video essays. Students learn how to use creative audiovisual media tools, in particular those related to the moving image. Students gain familiarity with digital production and editing technology, which they use as instruments of critical expression and argumentation.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Shakespeare and His Contemporaries
courses.description: This course explores the wide range of drama produced in England between the 1570s and 1640s, including work by Shakespeare and his many rivals. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Renaissance Literature and Its Intellectual Contexts
courses.description: An introduction to one or two intellectual movements of the Renaissance, such as humanism, the protestant reformation, the baroque, or the scientific revolution, through the examination of both literary and non-literary texts of the period.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Medieval Feminisms
courses.description: This course explores the contributions of the Middle Ages, and of medieval women, to the history of feminism and women's writing. Over the course of the semester, we will explore four different types of work by and about women: literary writing, theological writing, life writing, and the performance of identity and dramatic character. Along the way, we will also read selections from contemporary feminist theory, including Sara Ahmed, Lauren Berlant, Luce Irigaray, and Judith Butler.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Perspectives on the Renaissance
courses.description: Students will study Renaissance literature through one or more contemporary theoretical lenses, which might include feminist theory, queer theory, cultural materialism, new historicism, or psychoanalytic theory. Texts may range in date from the early 16th century to the late 20th and early 21st century.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: 18th-Century Literature
courses.description: A survey of British literature from Dryden to Paine. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: The Romantic Revolution in the Arts
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course examines the technical and aesthetic revolutions in the fine arts of the English Romantic Period. It will discuss productions, experiments, and aesthetic theories of William Wordsworth, S. T. Coleridge, J. M. W. Turner, and William Blake, focusing on the developments of lyrical poetry, landscape painting, and original printmaking. We will pay special attention to the period's new ideas about nature, the sublime, picturesque travel, genius, originality, and social role of the artist.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Tabletop Games: Narrative, History, and Design
courses.description: This course introduces students to developments in modern tabletop gaming. Students will analyze the mechanics and thematics that tabletop games use to create narratives. Particular attention will be paid to the values and stories that emerge from the decisions made by designers. This course culminates in a capstone project in which students create their own tabletop game. No prior experience with tabletop gaming is required.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: U.S. Literature on Page and Screen
courses.description: This course pairs selected canonical works of U.S. literature (short stories, poems, essays, and short novels) with films that adapt or translate the original text for cinema. Works range from westerns and war movies to psychological thrillers, biopics, and comedies. By comparing text and film, the course deepens students' understanding of both aesthetic forms and traces the sometimes conflicting ideals, myths, and narratives that gave shape to different historical versions of American national identity. Honors version available.

source.text: ENGL 346. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENGL 105 or ENGL 105I . | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: From Manuscript to Press: Writer as Publisher
courses.description: Students learn the basics of book production, including acquisitions, developmental editing, copy editing, layout and book design, marketing, and digital publication by working on titles in production at a national press and meeting with professionals in the industry.

source.text: ENGL 351. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, ENGL 130 , 131 , 132H , 133H , or 138 . | FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: British and American Fiction Since World War II
courses.description: Course studies contemporary British and American fiction through representative works. Intellectual and aesthetic, historical and cultural emphases. May include works from the Anglophone diaspora. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: 20th-Century British Literature and Culture
courses.description: This course examines factors shaping British/Commonwealth literature in the 20th century, especially the world wars and the dismantling of the British Empire. We will investigate themes of both nostalgia and anticipation: ways of remembering the past of England and the Empire, and of describing the future of British culture(s).

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Contemporary US Poetry
courses.description: This course focuses on important poets and poetic trends in the United States in the 21st century. It addresses how poems create space for marginalized, unacknowledged, suppressed, or completely unfamiliar perspectives. The class explores how social and cultural conditions both limit and enable poetic expression; how poets engage in political movements or modes of social critique; and how they work to build community across differences. The course seeks to develop reading skills that are crucial for interpreting poetry; to strengthen writing and oral communication skills; and to develop research skills.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Latina Feminisms: Civil Rights, Ecofeminism, and Health Studies
courses.description: This course will offer a theoretical grounding on Latina feminism and the historical moments and movements that inspired and/or influenced such Latina feminist thought and productions. In this course, we will gain a foundation for how Latina feminists theorize about gender, race, sex, culture, history, and aesthetics. We will analyze a variety of literary forms and genres (e.g., poems, essays, novels, plays, testimonios) and mediums (literature, film, documentaries, visual art).

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Contemporary Asian American Literature and Theory
courses.description: This course will explore contemporary Asian American literature and theory and will examine how Asian American literature fits into, yet extends beyond, the canon of American literature.

source.text: ENGL 360. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | ASIA 360 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Asian American Women's Writing
courses.description: This course covers writings by Asian American women and examines issues of gender, race, and sexuality.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Asian American Literature and History
courses.description: This course focuses on events of particular import in Asian American history and how they are recounted in a variety of interdisciplinary texts. Events may include the Japanese American incarceration, refugee movements, immigration, or others, at the instructor's discretion. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Feminist Literary Theory
courses.description: Theories of feminist criticism in relation to general theory and women's writing. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Migration and Globalization
courses.description: Covers literary works associated with one or more of the major historical migrations, forced and voluntary, and present-day works engaged with globalization.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: African American Literature to 1930
courses.description: Survey of writers and literary and cultural traditions from the beginning of African American literature to 1930. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: African American Literature, 1930-1970
courses.description: Survey of writers and literary and cultural traditions from 1930 to 1970. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: African American Literature, 1970 to the Present
courses.description: Survey of writers and literary and cultural traditions from 1970 to the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Race, Health, and Narrative
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course explores how issues of health, medicine, and illness are impacted by questions of race in 20th-century American literature and popular culture. Specific areas covered include pain, death, the family and society, reproduction, mental illness, aging, human subject experimentation, the doctor-patient relationship, pesticides, and bioethics. Honors version available.

source.text: ENGL 370. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: The Place of Asian Americans in Southern Literature
courses.description: This course will consider the themes of globalization and regionalism through an examination of narratives featuring Asians/Asian Americans in the American South. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Southern American Literature
courses.description: An introduction to Southern literature, with emphasis on the 20th-century: fiction, poetry, drama, essays. Representative authors include Faulkner, Wolfe, Williams, Warren, Hurston, Wright, Ransom, Tate, Welty, Chappell, McCullers, O'Connor. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Southern Women Writers
courses.description: The study of fiction, poetry, plays, and essays by Southern American women writers of the past 200 years, continuing to the present.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to the Celtic Cultures
courses.description: A broad survey of the cultures of the Celtic-speaking areas, notably Ireland, Wales, Scotland, and Brittany, with special emphasis on language and literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Film Criticism
courses.description: An introduction to the history and practice of film criticism.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Topics In Film History
courses.description: This course examines one or more topics in film history, focusing on specific periods. The scope may be national or transnational. Films are analyzed for how they address and reflect key historical developments. Restricted to any undergraduate student who is a Sophomore, Junior, or Senior with a GPA or 3.0 or higher, OR any First-Year student. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature and Cinema
courses.description: The course introduces students to the complex narrative, aesthetic, and rhetorical relationship between literature and cinema. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature and Media
courses.description: This course investigates the rich and complex relationship between literature and other mass media. Previously offered as ENGL 281. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Podcasting
courses.description: This class studies the composition and development of podcasts, paying attention to the unique affordances and drawbacks of podcast technologies. Students develop, research, script, and record podcasts in several genres, including topical, interview, and storytelling formats, while learning practical editing techniques using industry-standard software.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature and Law
courses.description: Explores various connections of literature and law, including literary depictions of crime, lawyers, and trials; literary conventions of legal documents; and/or shared problems in interpretation of law and literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Gender, Sexuality, and the South Asian Diaspora
courses.description: This course explores how gender and sexuality shapes the literature, politics, and public culture of South Asian immigrant communities in Europe, Africa, the Americas, and other locations outside the Indian subcontinent.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Canadian Literature
courses.description: A study of Canadian literature in English from the late 18th century to the present, with emphasis on 20th-century writing and on the novel.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Modernism: Movements and Moments
courses.description: What was modernism? When was modernism? Where was modernism? Reading literature and visual art from 1890 to 1940 in Europe, America, and Africa will be key to finding answers.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Major Film Directors
courses.description: This course introduces students to the aims and concerns of authorship study in film through discussion of a major filmmaker's body of work. The course may focus predominantly on a single figure or may compare two or more figures who share certain affinities of theme or style.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Literary Topics
courses.description: An intensive study of a single writer, group, movement, theme, or period. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Storytelling in Film and TV
courses.description: This course is dedicated to the study of key concepts of storytelling through theoretical readings and the media of film and TV. To learn the concepts, students will engage in analyses of filmed scenes and screenplays, and they will write scripted scenes. At the end of the semester, students will have written three 5-page analytical essays, an outline for a 4-scene act, and four contiguous screenplay scenes that, together, make up an act. For the final exam, students will present their revised four-scene act as a portfolio and will read an excerpt to the class.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Professional Writing Portfolio Development and Publication
courses.description: Students research, refine, and compose a portfolio of advanced written, oral, and multimedia work for professional audiences or publication. Each portfolio will contain an array of work that demonstrates the student's versatility as a writer, speaker, researcher, and/or editor. The portfolio is intended for presentation to professional audiences, potential employers, prospective graduate programs, and/or publication. Previously offered as ENGL 492.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Misbehaving Bodies: Dis/ease, Dis/order, & Dys/topia in Latinx Fiction and Film
courses.description: This course explores how Latinx fiction and film portray diasporic ''misbehaving'' bodies. We will explore how bodies not conforming to desired ''norms'' are treated both within global society and within their own multi-ethno-racial diasporic communities. The ''norms'' Latinx individuals and communities navigate are often invisible but clearly defined through language, policy/policing, social structure, and cultural production. The Latinx diaspora includes the United States, the Caribbean Basin, and other sites beyond the North Atlantic region.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Directed Readings in English or Creative Writing
courses.description: Permission of the department. Intensive reading on a particular topic under the supervision of a member of the staff.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Cinema and the Museum
courses.description: Museums have long been considered repositories for artifacts and sites of pedagogy, far removed from contemporary visual practices. And yet, today's museums are full of moving images, from interactive displays to IMAX theaters to screen-based art. In this class we will consider interactions between the cinema and the museum. Topics to be addressed include immersive viewing technologies, film and ethnography, expanded cinema, virtual reality, and installation art. This course includes visits to campus museums.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Composition for Teachers
courses.description: This course combines frequent writing practice with discussions of rhetorical theories and strategies for teaching writing. The course examines ways to design effective writing courses, assignments, and instructional materials.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Investigations in Academic Writing and Writing Centers
courses.description: This course considers learning to write from three vantage points: personal, social, and contextual. Emphasis on theory, reflective practice, and pedagogy for peer tutoring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Rhetoric in the Museum
courses.description: A course focused on research, writing, and engagement with museum exhibits focused on art or other collections. Students will practice rhetorical analysis and close looking with a special focus on works at a curated museum installation. Includes collaborative and individual research projects. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Creative Nonfiction
courses.description: In addition to surveying key works of creative nonfiction throughout the ages - from Montaigne in the 16th century to Solnit, Rankine, and Urrea in the 21st - we will be composing (and peer-reviewing) our own explorations of every subgenre, including memoir, literary journalism, travel writing, flash nonfiction, and the lyric essay, with an eye toward publication.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Fiction Writing
courses.description: A continuation of the intermediate workshop with emphasis on the short story and novella. Extensive discussion of student work and revisions in class and in conferences with instructor. Permission of the program director.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENGL 206, ENGL 210, ENGL 211, ENGL 212, or ENGL 214.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Advanced Poetry Writing
courses.description: Permission of the program director. A continuation of the intermediate workshop, with increased writing and revising of poems. Extensive discussion of student poetry in class and in conferences with instructor.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Collaboration: Composers and Lyricists
courses.description: This is a course in popular-songwriting collaboration, a workshop with constant presentation of original songs and close-critiquing of these assignments. Varied assignments including songs for soloists, duos, trios, quartets, and chorus; ballads, folk, jazz, blues, art, and musical-theater songs, etc.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Lyrics and Lyricists: A Collaborative Exploration of the Processes of Popular-Song Lyric Writing
courses.description: This course is a collaborative exploration of popular-song lyric writing, requiring numerous drafts written to varied existing musical models - narrative ballads; hymns; folk, theater, jazz, art, R&B, R&R, and worldbeat songs, etcetera - to be tried out and worked on in class, as well as in conference.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Documentary Film
courses.description: This course provides a history of documentary cinema since the beginnings of the medium and surveys different modes and theoretical definitions; or the course may focus largely on a certain mode (such as ethnographic, observational, first-person, cinema vérité, politically activist, found footage compilation, or journalistic investigation). Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Composing for Clients: Technical Communication Practicum
courses.description: This advanced technical communication course will help you develop skills in developing professional communication with a focus on developing written and oral communications for clients, user experience, project management, and technical editing. You will assess the communications needs for a client, develop a communication plan to fulfill that need, and then produce polished, professional deliverables for that client, including oral communication. You will also practice presenting communication plans and final documents orally to clients.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Sketch Comedy Writing
courses.description: This course provides a rigorous introduction to comedy arts, focusing on the individual and collaborative writing processes of sketch comedy. Students will learn to develop characters, settings, and tension using the tools preferred by contemporary performers, including the game of the scene, absurdity and incongruity, status, active patterning, and parody. This intensive experience culminates in student-written, live sketch comedy performances.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENGL 259 or 308; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENGL 412. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENGL 259 or 308 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature, Archives, and Original Research
courses.description: "Archives" are documents - manuscripts, photographs, recordings, diaries, letters, and other materials - that are so valuable they need to be preserved in a special place. In this course, the instructor will guide students as they conduct original research in literary archives, such as online databases or physical archives (at Wilson Library, for example). We will learn how to formulate research questions and how to identify key documents. Previously offered as ENGL 342.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Renaissance Literature--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: This course examines Renaissance literature through the lens of cultural themes, issues, and problems that were important to Renaissance authors and readers. Texts may be drawn from, among others, the English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish literary traditions, and may range in date from the 15th to the 17th centuries.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Chief British Romantic Writers
courses.description: Survey of works by Blake, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Percy and Mary Shelley, Keats, and others. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Literature before 1860--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: A junior- or senior-level course devoted to in-depth exploration of an author, group of authors, or topic in American literature to 1860. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Literature, 1860-1900--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: Intensive study of one or more authors or a topic in American literature from the Civil War through 1900. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Literature, 1900-2000--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: A junior- or senior-level course devoted to in-depth exploration of an author, group of authors, or a topic in American literature from 1900 to 2000. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Women Authors
courses.description: American women authors from the beginnings to the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Memory and Literature
courses.description: This course brings together theories of collective and individual memory with questions of aesthetics and narrative while exploring global connections between memory and literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Retro Aesthetics from Teen Films to Period Pieces
courses.description: Through analyses of teen and period films, this course explores cinema's relationship to time, memory, nostalgia, adolescence, aging, and history. It also examines the material specificity of film and its visual and sonic technologies, both analog and digital. Particular attention is given to retro aesthetics--tendencies that recall and rework the historical past.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Latinx Hybrid Narrative: Experimental Fiction and Film
courses.description: Latinx narrative in fiction and film has continually challenged the form and function of "genre". This course will examine books, films, and videos that are narrative in nature. We will focus on cultural productions reflecting some of these innovations to consider how authors and film makers engage concerns intersecting at different points of self-conception, including but not limited to experiences of dis/ability, diaspora, gender, geography, race, nationality, sexuality, spirituality, and transnationalism.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literary Theory--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: Examines current issues in literary theory such as the question of authorship, the relation of literary texts to cultural beliefs and values, and to the formation of identities. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Educating Latinas/os: Preparing SLI Mentors
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Designed for students accepted as mentors to the Scholars' Latino Initiative (SLI). Students will take this course during their first year as SLI mentors to prepare them as effective mentors to Latina/o high school students. Students cannot receive credit for both ENGL 267 and 467 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: African American Literature--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: Study of particular aspects of African American literature, such as the work of a major writer or group of writers, an important theme, a key tradition, or a literary period. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: The Changing Coasts of Carolina
courses.description: A rigorous combination of field work, lab work, and colorful, original contemporary writing on the natural world will help tell the story of our many, evolving North Carolina coasts. Combining marine science and the creative literary arts, this immersive course will explore issues of change over many eras. This combination of social, cultural, and scientific observation will lead to imaginatively constructed, well-written non-fiction reportage about one of North America's most productive, compelling, and challenging regions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Southern Literature--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: The study of a particular topic or genre in the literature of the United States South, more focused than students will find in ENGL 373 .
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Digital Humanities History and Methods
courses.description: Students will explore the history of computer-assisted humanities scholarship, from its beginnings in computational linguistics, media studies, and humanities computing to its current incarnation as "digital humanities." The course will provide an introduction to the field and to digital research methodologies and prepare students to develop their own digital projects. Previously offered as ENGL 530.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Metadata, Mark-up, and Mapping: Understanding the Rhetoric of Digital Humanities
courses.description: This Course-based Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) course interrogates the rhetoric of data construction and management by positioning students as "critical makers" in a digital humanities project. Previously offered as ENGL 353.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Critical Theory of Games
courses.description: A research-based course in which students are introduced to recent developments in the field of critical theory of games, and how thinkers in the public humanities draw on games to ask and answer questions in theoretical realms such as narrative, agency, language, identity, rhetoric, and economics. The course will culminate in a capstone digital humanities project in which students share their original research as a podcast. No gaming experience or equipment is needed.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Everyday Stories: Personal Narrative and Legend
courses.description: Oral storytelling may seem old-fashioned, but we tell true (or possibly true) stories every day. We will study personal narratives (about our own experiences) and legends (about improbable, intriguing events), exploring the techniques and structures that make them effective communication tools and the influence of different contexts and audiences.

source.text: ENGL 487. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | FOLK 487 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Critical Security Studies
courses.description: Introduces major topics in the interdisciplinary field of critical security studies. Critically analyzing the public construction of risk and security in military, technological, informational, and environmental domains, the course explores major theories that attempt to make sense of the transnational proliferation of violence and risk in historical and contemporary contexts.

source.text: ENGL 488. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | PWAD 484 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Science, Medicine, and Cultural Studies--Contemporary Issues
courses.description: The student will have an opportunity to concentrate on researching topics and texts central to the study of health, medicine, culture, and ethics. Central topics may include representations of genetics, cloning, reproduction, and biotechnology. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creative Writing: Special Topics
courses.description: Permission of the program director. An occasional advanced course, which may focus on such topics as advanced creative nonfiction, editing and publishing, the lyric in song and collaboration between lyricists and composers, the one-act play, and short-short fiction.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Research Methods in Film Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to research methods in film studies. While this course will provide a broad survey of methods one might employ in film studies research of all kinds, the course may be restricted to a particular research topic.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: ENGL 494. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Mentored Research
courses.description: Recommended for students in junior or senior year of study. Intensive mentored research, service learning, field work, or creative work. Requires 30 hours of research, writing, or experiential activities, culminating in a written project.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Literature
courses.description: Examines the ways knowledge from other disciplines can be brought to bear in the analysis of literary works. Questions of disciplinary limits and histories will also be addressed.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Drama on Location
courses.description: Offered as part of summer study abroad programs in Oxford, London, and Stratford-on-Avon. Students experience plays in performance and as texts, and discuss their literary, dramatic, cultural, and historical aspects. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Internship in Health Humanities
courses.description: An opportunity to gain credit for an internship in a field related to the study of health humanities, such as science writing, health non-profit work, and qualitative research. Available to majors with at least a 3.0 GPA. Requirements include regular journal entries, meetings with a faculty advisor, and a final report of 10-15 pages.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Practicum in Health Humanities
courses.description: This course introduces advanced undergraduate and graduate students to topics, methods, and concepts in health humanities through practical learning experiences.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Narrative, Literature, and Medicine: Advanced Interdisciplinary Seminar
courses.description: Sociologist Arthur Frank asserts that "whether ill people want to tell stories or not, illness calls for stories." This seminar explores narrative approaches to suffering, healing, and medicine's roles in these processes. Students learn literary and anthropological approaches to examine medically themed works from a range of genres.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: ENGL 611. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Survey of Old and Middle English Literature
courses.description: An introduction to English literature from the eighth to the 15th century, focusing on the primary works of Old English and Middle English literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Old English Language and Literature
courses.description: Students will learn to read Old English, the Germanic language spoken by the Anglo-Saxons in Britain from about the middle of the fifth century until the time of the Norman Conquest. Students will study Beowulf, "Caedmon's Hymn", and other selections in poetry and prose.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Arthurian Romance
courses.description: British and continental Arthurian literature in translation from the early Middle Ages to Sir Thomas Malory.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Shakespeare and His Contemporaries
courses.description: This course will examine drama written and performed in England from 1570 to 1640, situating Shakespeare's plays in relation to others in his generation.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: 19th-Century Women Writers
courses.description: An investigation of important texts by 19th-century women writers that considers issues of gender in relation to other important considerations--tradition, form, culture--with an introduction to the chief scholarly and critical problems of this period.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: War in 20th-Century Literature
courses.description: A study of literary works written in English concerning World War I, or the Spanish Civil War and World War II, or the Vietnam War. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: War in Shakespeare's Plays
courses.description: The focus is on Shakespeare's various treatments of war in his plays: all his Roman histories, most of his English histories, all his tragedies, even some of his comedies.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Literary Theory
courses.description: Examines contemporary theoretical issues and critical approaches relevant to the study of literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: History of Literary Criticism
courses.description: A history of literary criticism from the Greeks to mid-20th century, focusing on recurrent concerns and classic texts that are indispensable for understanding the practice of literary criticism today.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Queer Latina/o Literature, Performance, and Visual Art
courses.description: This course explores literature, performance art, film, and photography by Latinas and Latinos whose works may be described as "queer" and that question terms and norms of cultural dominance.

source.text: ENGL 665. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | WGST 665 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Queer Latina/o Photography and Literature
courses.description: This course explores Latina/o literature about photography in relation to photography by "queer" Latina/o artists and, through this double focus, poses certain questions about identity, subjectivity, and culture.

source.text: ENGL 666. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | WGST 666 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Marx and Marxist Theory
courses.description: This mixed graduate and undergraduate course introduces students to the basic elements of the thought of Karl Marx and the reception and transformation of these elements in later philosophies and theories of culture. In addition to the work of Marx, students may expect to read work by such thinkers as G. W. F. Hegel, W. E. B. DuBois, Rosa Luxembourg, Antonio Gramsci, Fredric Jameson, Sylvia Federici, Michel Foucault, C. L. R. James, and others.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Debates in Contemporary Theory
courses.description: This mixed graduate and undergraduate course selectively surveys recent contemporary theory by asking how certain debates, controversies, or conversations have shaped the terrain of literary and cultural studies in the present day. Though the particular topic of the course will vary, select iterations may involve the diachronic study of influence; the apposition of different methodological approaches; or the survey of recent work in a given area, such as affect theory or postcolonial studies.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Being and Race in African American Literature
courses.description: An examination of phenomenology, the "philosophy of experience." Taking the perspective that literature helps clarify our experience, we will engage in readings of various genres--poetry, autobiography, fiction, and drama--as we examine how literature not only records experience, but also shapes it through a distinct method of reasoning.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Digital Literature
courses.description: Digital literature explores how literary works are composed for, shaped by, and studied in electronic environments. Course texts range from books to electronic fiction and poetry to video games. Hands-on activities give students a chance to develop their own literary projects--either as electronic literary works or as digital scholarship.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Teaching Online
courses.description: This course explores issues and methodologies related to online teaching. Topics include instructor-student dynamics in the online classroom, opportunities for extending the classroom through online platforms, trends in online pedagogy, and development of online teaching portfolios.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Digital Editing and Curation
courses.description: Students will investigate theories and practices of editing in multimedia, digital environments. Students will explore histories of textual editing, research major humanities projects, examine trends and toolsets related to developing scholarly digital materials, and collaborate with one another and with campus entities to develop an online digital humanities project.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Film Theory
courses.description: This course provides a rigorous introduction to various theories (aesthetic, narrative, historical, political, psychological, philosophical) inspired by cinema.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Film and Media
courses.description: This course examines aesthetic and social aspects of contemporary cinema, television, and/or other media. Previously offered as ENGL 580. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature of the Americas
courses.description: Multidisciplinary examination of texts and other media of the Americas, in English and Spanish, from a variety of genres. Two years of college-level Spanish or the equivalent recommended but not required.

source.text: ENGL 685. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | CMPL 685 .

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Queer LatinX Environmentalisms
courses.description: This mixed level undergraduate and graduate student course examines queer LatinX literature from the 1970s to the present as it intersects with ecological and environmental concerns. We pay close attention to LatinX cultural productions that approach ecology and environmental justice from queer perspectives and that queer ecological concerns from minoritized perspectives.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in literary studies, composition, digital media, and related fields. Topic varies by semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: English Senior Honors Thesis, Part I
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. First semester of senior honors thesis. Independent research under the direction of an English department faculty member.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: English Senior Honors Thesis, Part II
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. Second semester of senior honors thesis. Essay preparation under the direction of an English department faculty member.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creative Writing Senior Honors Thesis, Part I
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. The first half of a two-semester seminar. Each student begins a book of fiction or creative nonfiction (25,000 words) or poetry (1,000 lines). Extensive discussion of student work in class and in conferences.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, ENGL 130, 131, 132H, 133H, or 138; and ENGL 206, 207, or 208; and ENGL 404, 406, 407.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creative Writing Senior Honors Thesis, Part II
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. The second half of a two-semester seminar. Each student completes a book of fiction, creative nonfiction, or poetry. Extensive discussion of student work in class and in conferences with instructor.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Guides students through the processes of developing an original research topic, conducting research, and analyzing research, leading students to produce a high-quality presentation of their findings. Topic varies by instructor but may focus on literary studies or closely-related arenas such as medical humanities, digital humanities, and creative writing, among others.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Medieval Studies
courses.description: Introduction to medieval studies for graduate students in any department. Intended to expose students to research problems, tools, and techniques in fields other than their own.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Rhetorical Theory and Practice
courses.description: A study of rhetorical theories and practices from classical to modern times. Emphasis is on translation of theories into instructional practice for teaching in the college writing classroom.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Technologies of Literary Production
courses.description: This course introduces the history of technologies used to produce and circulate literature, from medieval Europe to the twenty-first-century. Proceeding chronologically, this history provides a broad overview of the material conditions of possibility for the emergence of literary form and genre in the Anglophone tradition.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Humanities
courses.description: This course provides students with an introduction to the landscape of digital humanities history, theories, tools, and methods with a focus on humanities data. We will explore the affordances and constraints of approaches to humanities data in archives and metadata, text analysis, data visualization, mapping, and game studies. Within each of these areas, students will assess leading theories and learn hands-on tools and methods in order to create a digital humanities seminar paper on a topic of their choosing.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Old English Grammar and Readings
courses.description: An introduction to Old English language and literature that also attempts to relate that language to Modern English and to the larger context of the history of the English language.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Old English Poetry
courses.description: Required preparation, a working knowledge of Old English. The translation and interpretation of Old English poetry including works such as The Wanderer, The Seafarer, Deor, The Dream of the Rood, and Beowulf.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Later Middle English Literature
courses.description: English literature of the late 14th and 15th centuries, including Gower, the English and Scottish Chaucerians, and Sir Thomas Malory.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Chaucer
courses.description: A study of Chaucer's major poetry, including Troilus and Criseyde, at least some of the 'dream' poems such as Parliament of Fowls, and most of The Canterbury Tales.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in the American Novel
courses.description: A wide-ranging, graduate-level survey of the American novel from the late 18th century through the 20th century.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in American Poetry
courses.description: A wide-ranging, graduate-level survey of American poetry from the late 18th century through the 20th century.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
courses.description: An introduction to myriad texts, topics, controversies, institutions, and personalities that make up the ongoing knowledge projects that are loosely affiliated under the rubric "cultural studies."

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Methods in Health Humanities
courses.description: Permission of the Instructor. This course introduces students to topics and methods in health and humanities. Students will read classics in the field, engage texts from different disciplines and genres, and conduct intensive research into a condition or disability of their choosing.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Medicine Without Borders
courses.description: This course examines texts by medical professionals who practice in perilous venues, as well as their sponsoring institutions (Christian missions, the Red Cross, and Doctors Without Borders), investigating the texts' representational strategies and the historical and ethical settings of both texts and institutions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Old Irish I
courses.description: The main emphasis of the course will be on mastering the basic grammar of the language. There will be some readings from selected Old Irish glosses and from Aislinge Oenguso.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Old Irish II
courses.description: Readings from a variety of genres of Old Irish literature: Stories from the Tain, Crith Gablach, Cambrai Homily, Early Irish Lyrics, Scela Mucce Meic Datho.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Proseminar in American Literature, Prior to the Civil War

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Study in English and Comparative Literature
courses.description: This course introduces students to the field of literary studies in English and comparative literature. Students will survey a range of approaches, methods, and controversies that have emerged from the field. The focus on critical and institutional histories will provide a foundation for graduate work and for developing professional objectives.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Research Methods in Composition and Rhetoric
courses.description: Course introduces graduate students to methodologies of research in the field of Rhetoric and Composition. Emphasis is on theoretical and practical concerns that improve teaching and help develop research agendas.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Rhetoric and Composition
courses.description: Focus varies by semester, but generally investigates intersections of literacy, pedagogy, and rhetorical theory. Courses range from explorations of technology and literacy, to investigations of forms of writing and pedagogy.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: History of the English Language
courses.description: Study of English from its Proto-Indo-European origins through the 18th century focusing on historic events and the major changes to the structure and usage of English they occasioned.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Old English Language and Literature
courses.description: Topics in Old English poetry and prose that vary with each seminar and instructor.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Middle English Literature
courses.description: Intensive study of major Middle English authors or genres or of medieval cultural influences. Topics have included Malory, Piers Plowman and its tradition, drama, and intellectual backgrounds of medieval literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Renaissance Literature in Context
courses.description: A study of select works of Renaissance literature, both dramatic and nondramatic, in its intellectual, social, political, or religious context.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Renaissance Authors
courses.description: Concentrated studies of single authors, groups of authors thematically linked, or authors in their families or coteries.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Perspectives on Renaissance Literature and Culture
courses.description: Students will study Renaissance literature while assessing the usefulness and status of a theoretical approach, such as feminist theory, queer theory, cultural materialism, new historicism, or psychoanalytic theory.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Renaissance Literature: Drama
courses.description: A study of Renaissance drama linked thematically, or framed by select cultural practices and historical issues.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Renaissance Literature: Primarily Nondramatic
courses.description: A focused examination of an aesthetic, historical, or theoretical problem in the study of Renaissance literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in 18th-Century Literature
courses.description: Selected topics in 18th-century literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: 18th-Century Fiction
courses.description: Studies in eighteenth-century fiction from Behn to Austen.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in English Literature, 1780-1832
courses.description: Sections: 1) Blake, Wordsworth, Coleridge, 2) Byron, Shelley, Keats. Examination of the major Romantic poets, supplemented by readings in other Romantic authors.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: 19th-Century British Novel
courses.description: Examination of important 19th-century British novels, such as those by Austen, Scott, Dickens, the Brontes, sensation novelists, Gaskell, Carroll, Thackeray, Eliot, Trollope, Doyle, Hardy, Meredith.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Victorian Literature: Poetry
courses.description: Study of Victorian poets, focused on a group or a topic, including figures such as Tennyson, the Brownings, Arnold, and the Pre-Raphaelites.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in 19th-Century Romanticism in England
courses.description: Topics concerning major authors and issues of the Romantic period.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Victorian Literature
courses.description: Topics concerning major authors and issues of the Victorian period.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in American Literature to 1860
courses.description: Topics vary: e.g., New England Puritanism, New England response to American literary nationalism; Emerson; Irving, Hawthorne, and Poe and the development of the American short story.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in American Literature, 1860-1900
courses.description: In-depth exploration for doctoral students of selected topics or authors in American Literature from 1860 to 1900.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in the American Novel
courses.description: Doctoral-level seminar in the selected topics or authors.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in English and American Poetry of the 20th Century
courses.description: Usually taught as a survey of major poets: Yeats, Frost, Stevens, Williams, Pound, Eliot, Auden, with some more recent poets.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Modern Drama
courses.description: Explores representative works of contemporary playwrights.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in 20th-Century English and American Literature
courses.description: Studies in special modern and/or contemporary topics; e.g., the Irish literary renaissance, Latina/o Studies, Asian American Studies, cultural, visual culture, postcolonial, gender, and/or ethnic studies, and British and/or American Literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in English and American Fiction of the 20th Century
courses.description: Usually taught as a survey of major writers: Joyce, Lawrence, Woolf, Hemingway, Faulkner, with some other writers.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in 20th-Century Literature, English and American
courses.description: Seminar examining issues in modern English and American Literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Literary and Cultural Theory
courses.description: Seminar with varying topics, focusing on recent developments in literary and cultural theory, including narratology, feminism, psychoanalysis, and postcolonial and materialist theory.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Cultural Studies
courses.description: Advanced exploration of myriad tests, topics, controversies, institutions, and personalities that make up the ongoing knowledge projects that are loosely affiliated under the rubric 'cultural studies.'

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Postcolonial Literature
courses.description: Course examines the shifting meanings of postcoloniality in 20th- and 21st- century literature from formerly colonized countries.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Latina/o Literature, Culture, and Criticism
courses.description: Representative work by Latina/o writers and critics in relation to major social and historical trends and critical models-border theory, biculturalism, mestizaje, tropicalization, diaspora, pan-latinidad, Afro-Latina/o disidentifications, and LatinAsia Studies.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: African American and African Diasporan Literature, 1930-1970
courses.description: Key writers within the context of selected literary, cultural, and critical traditions from 1930 to 1970.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in African American Literature
courses.description: An intensive study of a major writer or text, a group of writers or texts, or an important trend, tradition, or literary period.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in African American and African Diasporan Literature
courses.description: An intensive study of a particular aspect of African American literature, such as speculative fiction, subject formation, comparative diasporan literatures, gender issues, theoretical and critical approaches, or formal innovations.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature of the U.S. South: Special Topics
courses.description: An in-depth treatment of selected topics (e.g., the Southern Renaissance, postmodern southern fiction, the racial conversion narrative) in Southern literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Critical Race Theory-Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Seminar examines and engages with critical race theory and the various texts (narrative, cultural productions) that are in conversation with theories of race and that reflect representations of race.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Irish I
courses.description: An introduction to modern Irish grammar.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Irish II
courses.description: Readings in Modern Irish Literature.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Ireland in Modernity
courses.description: This course will examine the relationships between Irish writing, culture, and modernism, in the context of international developments in literature and art.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Cinema
courses.description: This course offers graduate students the opportunity to investigate, in a seminar setting, a particular subject within the domain of film studies.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Ecological Theory and Practice
courses.description: In-depth evaluation of ecological theory, ecocritical pedagogy, and literary criticism.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.description: Topics vary according to the needs and interests of the individual student and the professor directing the reading and writing project.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.
